title: Minervit AI Delivery Project Adapter
description: Versioned adapter contract. The adapter's optional top-level schemaVersion field declares the contract version it targets (current: 1.x). The CLI validates adapters against this schema at load time (stdlib-only validator; no third-party runtime dependency).

definitionOfDone.description: The definition of done: the named condition set enforced at the goal-completion transition and reported at the session Stop boundary. Read-side only: never materialized into a rendered lane adapter, so an absent key stays absent and upgrades drift nothing (the `autonomy` precedent). Conditions: scope_complete, tests_written, tests_green, review_clean, evidence_bound, pr_handed_off, board_updated. Enforcement defaults to `warn` for the first release; `block` is supported and tested. `pr_handed_off` passes when the PR is out of the lane's hands -- merged, auto-merge armed, or in the merge queue -- and NEVER requires waiting for a queued PR to land.

enforcement.description: Posture at the goal-completion transition. Default: warn -- the conditions are evaluated and reported, and a failing one does not refuse the transition. Set block to make a failing condition refuse; `done-check` exits 1 on a fail regardless of this setting, so a hook or CI job can enforce without changing it.

conditions.description: Per-condition enable/disable. The known ids are enumerated and additional keys are REFUSED, so `validate-adapter` rejects a typo like `tests_grean` at validation time rather than leaving it to be discovered whenever a done-related command next runs.

integrationBranch.description: The branch a PR must target to count as handed off. Defaults to laneStatus.integrationBranch, which itself falls back to latestCode.base. Never hardcoded to `main`.

schemaVersion.description: Adapter contract version this adapter targets (semver). Optional; current contract is 1.x.

_generated.description: Provenance stamped onto a rendered lane adapter (.minervit-ai-delivery.json) by render-adapters. Absent on hand-authored source adapters.

_framework.description: Client-facing framework release-track pin. Existing products default to stable/manual/dry-run when omitted.

version.description: Exact framework version or simple semver range. Empty means current local version until explicitly pinned.

responseGuard.description: Internal Stop-hook compatibility controls. Omitted adapters use advisory phrase telemetry and state-based Stop decisions.

highPrecisionPhraseChecks.description: Mode for the high-precision phrase tier. Defaults to blocking, unlike the standard tier: a check whose false-positive surface is structurally bounded is telemetry-only everywhere under an advisory default. Set to advisory to demote the whole tier for this project.

questionGuard.description: Mode for the AskUserQuestion PreToolUse guard. Defaults to advisory: the guard evaluates the question payload and logs what it finds without denying. Set to blocking to deny a continue-vs-stop direction menu raised while a goal is unmet -- note that the classifier still has known false positives on operator-owned approval questions, so blocking is an opt-in.

developmentEnvironment.description: Optional lane runtime compatibility contract. Use this to declare when Windows developers should run gates through WSL2 rather than native win32 shells.

planningArtifacts.description: Planning artifact paths. Path-typed fields must be relative and stay under the project root (no leading / or ~, no .. segments); the CLI also enforces this containment at runtime. scratchPaths is exempt because the framework default (~/.claude/plans/) is an intentionally external, home-directory scratch location.

enforcement.description: off = vanilla superpowers; observe = log-only; advise = warn at finalize/precheck (never blocks); block = reject a plan that is not parallel/tiered/autonomous, or that has no goal-prompt artifact shipped alongside it at build-ready.

autonomy.description: Standing autonomy directive controls. Absent (the default) is treated as ON: session-start surfaces (goal-kickoff-prompt, lane-start, context-bootstrap, autonomy-directive) emit the directive. Read-side only: never materialized into a rendered lane adapter, so upgrades drift nothing.

standingDirective.description: Set false to fully opt out of the standing autonomy directive for this lane.

fleet.description: Fleet Governor: cross-worktree lease coordination. Absent (the default) means enabled with block enforcement. Repos with no leases see no friction (the guard short-circuits on an empty lease store); once any lane holds a live lease, edits to its paths from any other lane are enforced. The guard covers the structured file-edit tools (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit); writes issued through Bash are not guarded in v1.

enabled.description: Set false to disable fleet lease claims and the fleet guard hook for this project.

enforcement.description: block: deny edits to foreign-leased paths (with runnable escapes). advise: allow and inject the conflict as hook context. observe: allow and log edit_would_block to fleet.log.

defaultTtlMinutes.description: Lease time-to-live when a claim does not pass --ttl-minutes. Default 240. Capped at 525600 (one year): larger values overflow datetime arithmetic in the liveness check, which would abort the whole conflict scan and stop enforcing every other live lease.

productDevelopment.description: Opt-in PM (product-management) surfaces: precise product-doc path globs a human doing product/backlog work may change without fighting the VERSION-bump contract. Fail-closed allowlist: the CLI loader rejects broad globs and accepts a surface ONLY when its fixed root sits under the docs/product/ product root, segment-bounded, and overlaps no framework/code/config/release root. Each surface is a relative path glob (no leading / or ~, no .. segments).

laneCoordination.description: Cross-lane coordination area. root/contractPath/boardPath/laneStatusDir are an allowlisted external path group (the coordination root can live outside a single project, e.g. ~/Projects/<org>), so they are exempt from the project-root containment applied to other path fields.

goalTracker.description: DEPRECATED: superseded by `backlogProvider`. Retained for backward compatibility; the CLI warns at render time when an adapter still declares it. Migrate to `backlogProvider`.

provider.description: Backlog board provider id, validated against the provider registry rather than a closed enum, so a second board system is a registration and not a fork. Membership is checked in code because JSON Schema cannot express "is in the registry". A registered provider that does not yet serve a board verb refuses BY NAME when that verb is reached -- declaring a provider and implementing it are separate facts.

owner.description: GitHub Projects board owner. Required by the `github-projects` backlog provider only; each provider declares the fields that identify its board.

siteUrl.description: Jira Cloud site URL, e.g. https://your-team.atlassian.net. Required by the `jira` backlog provider.

projectKey.description: Jira project key, e.g. PROJ. Required by the `jira` backlog provider.

boardId.description: Jira board id, optional. Supplies rank ordering; without it board order falls back to a JQL ORDER BY Rank.

emailEnv.description: NAME of the environment variable holding the Jira account email. Never the value: the adapter is committed to a repository.

apiTokenEnv.description: NAME of the environment variable holding the Jira API token. Never the value: the adapter is committed to a repository.

allowRepoOnlyGoals.description: Allow a goal with no GitHub Project Source item to proceed repo-only instead of refusing. Off by default; the sanctioned path for work that legitimately has no board item.

unavailablePolicy.description: How board gates treat provider-unavailable (gh missing/unauthed/offline). block (default): an unreadable authoritative board fails the gate. warn: explicit opt-down for deliberate offline work.

provider.description: Backlog board provider id, validated against the provider registry rather than a closed enum, so a second board system is a registration and not a fork. Membership is checked in code because JSON Schema cannot express "is in the registry". A registered provider that does not yet serve a board verb refuses BY NAME when that verb is reached -- declaring a provider and implementing it are separate facts.

owner.description: GitHub Projects board owner. Required by the `github-projects` backlog provider only; each provider declares the fields that identify its board.

projectKey.description: Jira project key, e.g. PROJ. Required by the `jira` backlog provider.

emailEnv.description: NAME of the environment variable holding the Jira account email. Never the value: the adapter is committed to a repository.

apiTokenEnv.description: NAME of the environment variable holding the Jira API token. Never the value: the adapter is committed to a repository.

planRepo.description: Checkout holding this lane's plans when they live outside it; empty means lane-only. Its directory BASENAME is the plan-reference root token (tautline-backlog:ready/x/plan.md), resolved dynamically so no spelling is blessed. This is the one adapter path deliberately permitted to resolve OUTSIDE the project root: adapter paths are otherwise contained under it, which would refuse a sibling checkout before root resolution ran. The allowance is scoped to this key alone and is never a general escape. Independent of enabled, so a lane may keep plans externally while its board provider is off. Basename lane is refused as reserved.

allowRepoOnlyGoals.description: Allow a goal with no GitHub Project Source item to proceed repo-only instead of refusing. Off by default; the sanctioned path for work that legitimately has no board item.

completionUnit.description: The unit of completion for provider-backed work. `goal` preserves the legacy goal-ledger closeout model; `provider-item` makes the external issue/work item the completion object while repo plans and milestones decompose execution.

doneEvidence.description: Oracle discipline at closure: what the verification evidence posted with a done move must contain.

acTable.description: When the linked issue carries written acceptance criteria, require the done evidence to contain a line-by-line AC pass/fail table with one PASS/FAIL row matched to each criterion; a FAIL row refuses the move (an unmet criterion is a FAILED AC, never a deferral). `warn` (default) prints the finding and proceeds, `strict` refuses before any board mutation, `off` skips the check and its issue-body read. An unreadable issue body reports an explicit `unknown` state rather than passing silently.

allowedItemWrites.description: Per-field opt-in for normally-forbidden stakeholder-authored item writes (board-item-updates skill, Tier 2). All default false; omit the block for default-deny.

schemaHash.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the board schema at the time of the last board-adopt run. Written by backlog-board-adopt --apply; used by board_schema_changed to detect schema drift.

boardProfile.description: Freeform read-model snapshot of the board schema (status field, columns, single-selects, order candidates, custom fields) captured at the last board-adopt run. Written by backlog-board-adopt --apply.

unavailablePolicy.description: How board gates treat provider-unavailable (gh missing/unauthed/offline). block (default): an unreadable authoritative board fails the gate. warn: explicit opt-down for deliberate offline work.

workProfiles.description: Explicit local work-profile support. Default remains development; non-dev profiles are selected through a local lane-start profile lock.

T0.description: Legacy adapters may declare a positive T0 budget; runtime warns and coerces it to 0 because T0 does not use cross-model implementation review.

enforcement.description: off = the vendor-difference check does not run; observe = event-log record only; advise = warn and stamp the degradation into the manifest; block = refuse. Default block, which is strictly more permissive than the previous reviewer-must-be-codex rule.

derivedArtifacts.description: Committed artifacts generated from source files. record-stage1-sweep blocks (the machine-enforced derived-artifact freshness gate) when a declared artifact's sources changed in the reviewed base...HEAD diff without the artifact being regenerated in that same diff.

artifact.description: Repo-relative path of the committed derived artifact.

sources.description: fnmatch globs (repo-root-relative; '*' spans '/', so use '*' not '**') for the source files the artifact is generated from.

regenerate.description: Command that regenerates the artifact (surfaced in the block message).

deployHealth.description: Optional deployment workflow history gate. When enabled, Session Start runs deploy-health and blocks on latest failed deploy, repeated failures, no recent success, or unreadable deploy history.

outcomeSignals.description: Customer-outcome health contract (rec #1): real customer round-trips that prove a milestone-close deploy succeeded (e.g. 'guest places an order -> 201 and the order is visible'). A milestone-close target must declare at least one NON-proxy signal when healthContract.enforcement is block -- a proxy (/health, 200 OK, a DB read) does not count.

sideEffects.description: External side-effect delivery proof (rec #15): each declared outbound side-effect (email/sms/push/webhook/payment) needs a provider-RECEIPT proof, not an outbox row. Enforced when sideEffectProof.enforcement is block.

enforcement.description: Detection-baseline gate (rec #9). When block, `readiness-review` (or --strict) fails closed unless the default branch enforces required checks + strict protection, the canaryWorkflow's last run on the deployed SHA concluded success, and each alarmSources file wires an errorId/alarm. Default off.

requiredChecks.description: Status-check contexts branch protection must require.

canaryWorkflow.description: Name of the synthetic-canary workflow whose last conclusion on the deployed SHA must be success.

alarmSources.description: Repo files that must contain errorId/alarm wiring (so detection is not human-only).

testEvidence.description: Test-execution evidence (tautline-test-run/v1). Declares where the test runner writes its machine-readable report so `tautline test-run` can record real counts instead of exit-code-only evidence. Omitting it is valid: the record then carries counts.source=exit-code-only and says so, rather than claiming zeros.

report.description: The stable path the runner writes its report to (e.g. a --junitxml target). `test-run` copies it beside each record and hashes the copy, so a later run overwriting this path cannot invalidate an older record.

freshCheckout.description: Whether `tautline test-run` reproduces CI's checkout state by default: the gate runs in a throwaway checkout holding only what git can see, so gitignored runtime state cannot make a test pass locally and fail on every fresh clone. Omitting it keeps runs in place.

default.description: Default mode for `test-run` in this lane. `--fresh-checkout` / `--no-fresh-checkout` override it per run.

carryPaths.description: Gitignored dependency directories installed out-of-tree by CI (e.g. .venv, node_modules) that are symlinked into the fresh checkout so the configured gate can start. Relative to the project root; tracked paths are refused.

enforcement.description: How the prepush gate and finalize-implementation-review treat the tautline-test-run/v1 record. block (the default) refuses a push or a push-eligible review verdict unless the newest record is present, trustworthy, current to the tree being shipped, green, and proves tests actually executed; warn reports the same finding and changes no exit code; off is silent. A classifier internal error (unavailable) always fails OPEN, in every mode. Every block refusal prints its remedy.

mergeGate.description: Client-side merge gate: `tautline merge` verifies the PR's live check rollup before merging. Exists because branch protection and rulesets are paid features for private repositories, so the most common adopter configuration cannot have a required status check at all and CI gates nothing. Omitting the key leaves the gate advisory.

enforcement.description: off = no check; advise = warn on a red PR but merge; block = refuse, with `--override <reason>` as the recorded break-glass.

blockOnPending.description: Treat a check that has not reported yet as blocking. Defaults true: merging while checks are still running is how a red commit lands on a repo without platform enforcement.

postMergeTier.description: The post-merge acceptance suite on the integration branch -- the tier that tells you whether the branch you are merging INTO is red. `tautline base-health` reads it; session start, the pre-push hook, and `tautline merge` consult it. The verdict comes from a completed run on the base tip when one exists, else the newest completed run by creation time (commit order); an untested known tip is never green; marker issues are never an input; an unreadable tier is `unknown`, never green. Omitting the key disables it.

enforcement.description: off = never read; advise = report a red base but proceed; block = `tautline merge` and the pre-push hook refuse while the base is red, released only by a live fleet lease held by the merging worktree whose note starts with one of claimNotePrefixes, or by `--override <reason>`.

workflow.description: Workflow file or name, as `gh run list --workflow` accepts it.

branch.description: Branch the tier runs on. Defaults to the adapter's integration branch (laneStatus.integrationBranch, then latestCode.base).

limit.description: Runs to read per check. Default 20; must cover the longest plausible overlap of in-flight runs.

claimNotePrefixes.description: A live fleet lease owned by the merging worktree whose note starts with one of these releases the refusal: the lane fixing the red must be able to land the fix. Default `base-red claim:` and `main-red claim:`.

ciTestGate.description: CI/CD pipeline health check: verifies the repo's tests are actually run by CI on PR/push. Fails closed when tests exist but no workflow runs them.

expectTests.description: Whether this repo is expected to have an automated test suite. Defaults true when the adapter declares deploymentTargets. When no tests are detected (or the scan is inconclusive) and expectTests is true, the gate fails closed instead of self-disabling (FM2 fail-open closure). Set false to explicitly assert a deliberately test-less surface.

requiredCheckName.description: Name of the required CI status check (a GitHub Actions CheckRun name or a commit StatusContext context, e.g. a Jenkins-posted status). When set, branch_liveness fails closed if an OPEN PR's check of this name CONCLUDED a hard failure (FM3: a not-green PR is not active work). Opt-in: unset means no CI-conclusion blocking.

uiEvidence.description: Opt-in UI proof gate. When enabled with block enforcement, configured goal/work-item transitions require a Playwright screenshot evidence manifest (`minervit-ui-evidence/v1`) before completion, and may automatically post the manifest summary to the linked GitHub issue as proof.

runtimeConfig.description: Required-runtime-secret registry (FM3/P4, the #448 class). Declares secrets that MUST be present at runtime so a missing one fails the deploy loudly (boot fail-fast / secret-parity) rather than silently degrading to an empty string via the `?? ''` idiom. When enforcement is block, methodology-status --fail-on-drift fails on a degrade-to-empty read of a registered secret.

criticalJourneys.description: Declared load-bearing customer journeys. Each maps a journey name to the .feature files/globs that cover it. A scenario in any of these features must never be @pending (RC5): methodology-status --fail-on-drift fails on an inactive critical-journey scenario.

migrationSafety.description: Destructive-migration guard (FM1/data-durability). Opt-in via migrationsPath (a .sql file/dir/glob). A migration with un-guarded destructive DDL (DROP TABLE/COLUMN/CONSTRAINT, TRUNCATE, SET NOT NULL) must be reversible/expand-contract or carry a reviewed ackMarker comment, else methodology-status reports drift (blocking when enforcement is block).

coverageFloor.description: Diff-scoped coverage gate (rec #7 Part 2). The `diff-coverage-check` subcommand intersects the NEW lines a change adds (git diff against diffBase) with the executed lines in a coverage report (coverage.py JSON or LCOV) and fails when new-line coverage is below newCodeMinPct. Blocks only when enforcement is block; diff-scoped is the right instrument for new code (whole-repo fail_under is the coarse backstop).

planAcceptance.description: Acceptance-criteria-to-test binding gate (rec #13). When enforcement is block, plan-finalization-precheck fails any acceptance criterion under an acHeadings section that names no executable test/scenario id (test_*, *.feature, Scenario:, Test:/Verified by:, etc.) or is bound to an inactive (@pending) scenario. warn surfaces the same as non-fatal warnings; off disables. Definition-of-Ready with teeth.

flakyQuarantine.description: Quarantine forcing-function (rec #14). The `flaky-quarantine-check` subcommand fails a diff that ADDS a flaky/skip/xfail marker (markers, default a cross-stack set) without recording an owner AND a due/issue/trigger in the same hunk, so a quarantined test becomes tracked debt rather than silent gate erosion. When scanPath is set and maxMarkers>=0 it also enforces a repo-wide marker ratchet (lower maxMarkers as flakies are fixed; never raise). Blocks only when enforcement is block.

goLiveReadiness.description: Go-Live Readiness profile (policy 16a). live-tenant declares this lane serves a customer surface: each go-live control must reach its own satisfying state, or carry an explicitly recorded decline. That state is not uniform -- some controls take enforcement:block, while others are satisfied by populating what they measure (declared critical journeys, quarantine bounds and a scan path, alarm sources and required checks); adding an enforcement key to a control that has none makes the adapter schema-invalid, and methodology-status names the specific state each unsatisfied control needs. A milestone-close deploymentTarget without this profile is a warn today; it becomes drift only when goLiveReadiness.enforcement is set to block.

enforcement.description: Whether a milestone-close deploymentTarget WITHOUT profile live-tenant is drift. Default warn (advisory line only, never fails --fail-on-drift/--strict). Set block once this lane has adopted the profile.

control.description: A go-live control key as reported by control_posture (ciTestGate, healthContract, readiness, runtimeConfig.requiredSecrets, criticalJourneys, flakyQuarantine, remediation), or the literal 'goLiveReadiness.profile' to decline adopting the profile itself.

healthContract.description: Customer-outcome health contract (rec #1). When enforcement is block, methodology-status drift-fails any milestone-close deploymentTarget that declares no NON-proxy outcomeSignals entry -- green must mean a real customer round-trip passed, not a liveness proxy (P1 provability theater). off (default) disables; warn reports without failing.

sideEffectProof.description: External side-effect delivery proof (rec #15). When enforcement is block, methodology-status drift-fails any milestone-close deploymentTarget whose declared sideEffects lack a provider-receipt proof (an outbox row written/queued is not delivery). off (default) disables; warn reports without failing.

remediation.description: Open-remediation forcing function (rec #3). A committed obligation ledger (ledgerPath, a JSON list or {obligations:[...]} of {id, owner, due, status, verifiedBy}). methodology-status drift-fails (under --fail-on-drift, or always when enforcement is block) any obligation that is overdue and still open, or marked closed without a customer-outcome verify -- 'PR merged' is not proof a recurrence is fixed. No-op when the ledger file is absent.

redGreen.description: Red-green discrimination proof (rec #8). The `red-green-check` subcommand mutates one symbol of a changed source file and runs the test command; a surviving mutation proves the tests are no-ops (they would pass even if the code broke). Fails closed on a survivor when --strict or enforcement is block. A mutation that only breaks loading/collection is rejected as a kill (inconclusive, not a pass).

agents.description: Registry of agents this project may bind to a role. Keys are opaque agent ids chosen by the adopter.

vendor.description: Model provider. FREE-FORM: never an enum, never an allowlist. The framework compares two vendor strings for inequality and attaches no other meaning to the value.

runtime.description: Harness this agent runs in. FREE-FORM: determines which in-session enforcement is available, looked up as data in methodology/runtime-capabilities.json.

instructionFile.description: Generated instruction file for this agent, e.g. CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md. Replaces the hardcoded RUNTIME_TARGETS table.

transcriptMarker.description: Legacy fallback only: the speaker marker to scan for when this agent's wrapper does not emit structured output. Declared per agent, never assumed.

runtimeCapabilities.description: What in-session enforcement a runtime actually supplies, keyed by the `runtime` value an agent declares. WHOLE-ENTRY REPLACEMENT per runtime, adapter wins -- never a union with the shipped list, because an adopter whose harness dropped a hook must be able to say so. Runtimes not named here keep the shipped list from methodology/runtime-capabilities.json; a runtime named nowhere is reported as zero-capable, which is the safe default rather than the intended path. Reports only, never blocks.

roles.description: Per-seam role bindings. Each value must resolve to a key in `agents`.
